content.title: Additional measles public exposure locations confirmed in Coconino County • Coconino County, AZ
content.text: Coconino County Health and Human Services (CCHHS) has confirmed that a second Coconino County resident has tested positive for measles. Home Posted on March 30, 2026 Coconino County Health and Human Services (CCHHS) has confirmed that a second Coconino County resident has tested positive for measles. The first measles case of 2026 was announced on March 20, 2026.CCHHS is working with state and local partners to notify individuals who have potentially been exposed to illness. Individuals who were at the locations at the dates and times listed below may have been exposed and should monitor for any signs or symptoms of illness.Public exposure details for current confirmed measles case:LocationDateTimeWatch for symptoms through this datePage Unified School District school busRoute 3 & 6Stops at:- Page High- Manson Mesa High- Page Middle- Desert View Elementary- Lake View Primary- Page Early ChildhoodMon., March 23 Tues., March 24 Wed., March 25Morning and afternoon transportation timesApril 16, 2026Manson MesaHigh School500 S Navajo Dr.Page, AZ 86040Mon., March 23Tues., March 24Wed., March 257:30 a.m. – 5:40 p.m.April 16, 2026Tuba City Regional Health Care Emergency Room Department167 N Main St.Tuba City, AZ 86045Fri., March 2710:30 a.m. - 7 p.m. Tuba City 9:30 a.m. - 6 p.m. ArizonaApril 18, 2026Tuba City Regional Health Care Main Hospital Building167 N Main St.Tuba City, AZ 86045Fri., March 2710:30 a.m. - 12:45 p.m. Tuba City9:30 a.m. - 11:45 a.m. ArizonaApril 18, 2026Previous public exposure details for March 20, 2026, confirmed measles case: LocationDateTimeWatch for symptoms through this datePage High School, 434 S Lake Powell Blvd, Page, AZ 86040Thurs., March 127:30 a.m. – 5:40 p.m.April 2, 2026Safeway650 Elm St, Page, AZ 86040 Thurs., March 1212:30 – 3:00 p.m.April 2, 2026Banner Page Hospital501 N Navajo Rd, Page, AZ 86040Mon., March 1612:40 – 5:20 p.m. April 6, 2026Symptoms typically appear seven to 12 days after exposure but may take up to 21 days. Symptoms include:• High fever (> 101°F)• Cough• Feeling run down, achy (malaise)• Red, watery eyes (conjunctivitis)• Runny nose• Blotchy rash that usually starts on the face (starting at the hairline), extends down the body and can involve palms and solesTwo doses of the MMR vaccine are recommended by doctors as the best way to protect against measles, mumps, and rubella, starting with the first dose at 12 to 15 months of age, and the second dose at 4 through 6 years of age. Teens and adults should also be up to date on their MMR vaccination.Those experiencing fever, cough, runny nose, rash, or any other symptoms of measles should: Self-isolate, stay away from others, and contact your healthcare provider by phone. Let them know you are concerned you may have measles. They will provide instructions for you to visit their office at a time that will not risk exposing others.If you do not have a healthcare provider and need to seek care, please contact the urgent care or hospital by phone before visiting and let them know that you suspect measles. To seek medical care regarding measles at Tuba City Regional Healthcare, call 1-866-976-5941 before arrival. Prior to visiting Page Hospital, call (928) 645-2424.Individuals who are immunocompromised or have received only one dose of the MMR vaccine are at higher risk. Please consult your healthcare provider.Contact your healthcare provider or call the CCHHS Health and Wellness Clinic at (928) 679-7222 to schedule an MMR vaccination. To check your MMR status or if you have other questions, call the Tuba City Regional Health Care public health hotline at(928) 606-4647.Visit ADHS Measles Homepage for more information.# # # Related News
